messages:
jordan: Quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose a narrow refactor: replace our current fixed-window credit allocator with a lightweight sliding-credit curation layer that feeds the abuse detector and the fairness scheduler. This is to reduce transient tail latency and make abuse signals less noisy. thoughts? :thinking:

anya: curious — can you sketch the data flow? is this changing admission contracts or just telemetry we feed into abuse?

jordan: Mainly the allocator + telemetry. Admission API stays same for now (token request -> admit/deny). New piece sits upstream and maintains a decayed credit score per tenant that both the scheduler and abuse service can subscribe to.

samir: pros: faster reaction to spikes, smoother decay, cheaper than per-request token ledger. cons: counter drift, harder to reason about worst-case capacity. also cost of state if we keep many tenants hot.

lee: how does this interact with KV cache reuse? Sliding window may penalize workloads with long context reuse if credits decay too fast. We should tie decay to active-usage pulses, not wall clock only.

jordan: yes planning a hybrid pulse-aware decay. rough config proto:
```
sliding_credit: {
  window_ms: 60000,
  decay_alpha: 0.15,
  pulse_boost_ms: 300000,
  max_burst_tokens: 1200,
  min_reserve_pct: 0.02
}
```
This gives tenants a short-term smoothing window + an occasional pulse extension when requests are bursty (KV reuse case).

maria: for abuse model: will the detector take raw event counts or the smoothed credit score? we need to avoid double-penalizing noisy clients (credit drops -> probe -> more drops). propose the detector consumes both the raw rate and the smoothed credit and has a hysteresis gate.

ash (ash): idea: expose a "grace band" boolean for tenants in rollout so we can canary the new logic. If grace=true, scheduler uses old scoring for admission but we still emit new telemetry for offline eval.

jordan: strong +1 to canary/gate. plan: opt-in namespace flag and a global kill-switch via config. ops-bot, can we get a temporary metric tag for canary tenants?

ops-bot: created metric tag `sliding_credit_canary=true` for the next 72h. :white_check_mark:

samir: perf question — marshal state into rough buckets (hot/cold) or keep per-tenant float? buckets reduce memory but make tuning hairy. I'd lean per-tenant floats with TTL + LRU eviction.

lee: agree on per-tenant floats + ttl. Also we need deterministic reconciliation for multi-proxy paths: use monotonically increasing epoch on writes and last-writer-wins. avoid heavy coordination.

maria: test plan: 1) synthetic spike with KV reuse pattern 2) abuse-sim attacker flood 3) long-tail steady noisy tenant. Collect false-positive/false-negative rates vs current baseline. I can own eval harness.

jordan: perfect. deliverables: (1) small shim service that maintains sliding scores + exposes subscribe webhook + metrics, (2) admission hook toggle, (3) eval harness results. I'll draft a short RFC appendix with tradeoffs.

anya: timeline?

jordan: two-week spike: prototype + canary telemetry, four-week: canary rollout with graceband, eight-week: evaluate and decide on default flip.

ash (ash): one more thought — fallback policy when credit subsystem is degraded: fall back to current fixed-window allocator and emit high-priority alert. make it explicit in runbook.

jordan: good call. I'll add to runbook. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
